planDocument.title: Mac Counter QA - Plan Document
planDocument.markdown:
# Mac Counter QA - Plan Document

## 1. Overview
Mac Counter QA is a small React counter application for QA demonstration. It starts at 0 and provides increment, decrement, and reset controls with accessibility and responsive styling. No backend, login, external network, or persistent data is involved; a fresh preview always starts at 0.

## 2. Goals
- Provide a simple, reliable counter starting at 0.
- Demonstrate correct increment, decrement, and reset behavior.
- Enforce non-negative constraint (never below 0).
- Meet accessibility basics: aria-live polite, keyboard focus, semantic controls.
- Provide responsive styling for desktop and mobile.
- Enable Architecture and Workflow generation, then Build and Preview.

## 3. Non-Goals
- No backend, API, database, or server-side logic.
- No authentication, login, user accounts, or roles.
- No external network calls or third-party integrations.
- No persistent storage (localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies).
- No analytics, telemetry, or tracking.
- No multi-counter, history, undo, or advanced features.

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Functional Requirements
- R1: App displays a counter value starting at 0 on initial load and on fresh preview.
- R2: Increment button adds 1 to the counter on each activation.
- R3: Decrement button subtracts 1 but is disabled when counter is 0; counter never goes negative.
- R4: Reset button returns counter to 0 from any value.
- R5: Counter value is visibly displayed and updates immediately after each action.
- R6: All controls are usable via mouse/touch and keyboard (Tab, Enter/Space).

### 4.2 Accessibility & UX Requirements
- R7: Counter display uses aria-live="polite" to announce changes.
- R8: Buttons have accessible names, visible focus indicators, and proper disabled state for Decrement at 0.
- R9: Layout is responsive and readable on mobile and desktop viewports.
- R10: App has a clear title/heading identifying it as Mac Counter QA.

### 4.3 Technical Constraints
- R11: Implementation is React frontend only; no backend or persistent data.
- R12: Fresh preview/refresh always starts at 0 with no restored state.

## 5. Components and Boundaries

### 5.1 In Scope Components
- CounterApp (root component): holds count state (useState(0)), renders heading, display, and controls.
- CounterDisplay: presents current count with aria-live="polite" and aria-atomic="true".
- Controls: Increment, Decrement, Reset buttons with click handlers and disabled logic.
- Styles: responsive CSS (flex/grid, media queries) for layout and focus states.

### 5.2 Out of Scope / Boundaries
- No backend service, API layer, or database.
- No auth provider or session management.
- No network client or external fetch.
- No persistence adapter.

### 5.3 Data Flow
User action -> event handler -> setCount updater -> re-render -> CounterDisplay updates -> aria-live announcement.

## 6. Interfaces

### 6.1 User Interface
- Heading: "Mac Counter QA"
- Display: numeric value, aria-live="polite"
- Buttons: Increment (+1), Decrement (-1, disabled at 0), Reset (to 0)
- Keyboard: Tab to focus, Enter/Space to activate, focus ring visible.

### 6.2 Component Props/State (Conceptual)
- State: count: number (0..n, integer)
- Handlers: onIncrement(): setCount(c => c+1), onDecrement(): setCount(c => Math.max(0, c-1)), onReset(): setCount(0)
- Derived: isDecrementDisabled = count === 0

### 6.3 No External Interfaces
No REST, GraphQL, or storage interfaces.

## 7. Security Considerations
- No authentication or authorization required.
- No sensitive data handled.
- No external network reduces attack surface.
- Ensure no injection via display (render count as text, not HTML).
- No persistence means no data leakage across sessions.

## 8. Workflow, Dependencies, Parallel Work

### 8.1 Workflow Phases
1. Plan (this document) - requirements and acceptance defined.
2. Architecture and Workflow - derive component structure, state flow, styling approach.
3. Build and Preview - implement React components, compile, preview at 0.

### 8.2 Dependencies
- Architecture depends on Plan approval.
- Build depends on Architecture.
- Preview depends on successful Build/compile.

### 8.3 Parallel Work Opportunities
- Styling/responsive design can proceed in parallel with component logic.
- Accessibility attributes (aria-live, focus) can be added alongside button implementation.
- Acceptance checks can be drafted in parallel with Architecture.

## 9. Acceptance and Planned Tests

### 9.1 Acceptance Criteria
- A1: On load/fresh preview, counter displays 0.
- A2: Clicking Increment increases value by 1 each time (0->1->2).
- A3: Decrement is disabled at 0 and counter never shows negative; enabled when >0 and subtracts 1.
- A4: Reset returns any value to 0.
- A5: Counter display has aria-live="polite" (inspectable).
- A6: All buttons reachable and operable via keyboard with visible focus.
- A7: Layout remains usable on narrow (320px) and wide viewports.
- A8: No backend calls, no login UI, refresh returns to 0.

### 9.2 Planned Tests (Manual/Preview Checks)
- T1: Load app, verify 0 displayed, Decrement disabled.
- T2: Increment 3 times, verify 3; Decrement once, verify 2.
- T3: Decrement to 0, verify disabled and no negative on extra clicks/key presses.
- T4: Increment to 5, Reset, verify 0.
- T5: Keyboard-only: Tab through controls, activate with Enter/Space.
- T6: Inspect element for aria-live="polite" on display.
- T7: Resize viewport to 320px and 1024px, verify no overflow/cropping.
- T8: Refresh preview, verify returns to 0 (no persistence).

## 10. Assumptions
- React with functional components and hooks is acceptable.
- Standard build tooling (Vite/CRA/Next static) available for preview.
- No specific design system required; simple clean styling suffices.
- Browser support: modern evergreen browsers.

## 11. Risks and Rollback

### 11.1 Risks
- Risk: Decrement not properly disabled leading to negatives -> Mitigate with disabled prop + Math.max guard.
- Risk: aria-live missing -> Mitigate with explicit attribute and manual inspection.
- Risk: State persistence accidentally added -> Mitigate by prohibiting storage APIs.
- Risk: Responsive breakage -> Mitigate with flex layout and viewport testing.

### 11.2 Rollback
- No deployment rollback needed (frontend preview only).
- If Build fails, revert to last compiling commit; re-verify acceptance A1-A8.

## 12. Open Questions
None - requirements are clear for Architecture and Build phases.
